source_text: Τίνι οὖν, φημί, ἔτι τις χρήσαιτο διδασκάλῳ (??) πόθεν ὠφεληθείη τις. εἰ μηδὲ ἐν τούτοις τὸ ἀληθές ἐστιν; Ἐγένοντό τινες πρὸ πολλοῦ χρόνου πάντων τούτων τῶν νομιζομένων φιλοσόφων παλαιότεροι, μακάριοι καὶ δίκαιοι καὶ θεοφιλεῖς, θείῳ πνεύματι λαλήσαντες καὶ τὰ μέλλοντα θεσπίσαντες, ἃ δὴ νῦν γίνεται· προφήτας δὲ αὐτοὺς καλοῦσιν. Οὗτοι μόνοι τὸ ἀληθὲς καὶ εἶδον καὶ ἐξεῖπον ἀνθρώποις, μήτ᾿ εὐλαβηθέντες μήτε δυσωπηθέντες τινά. μὴ ἡττημένοι δόξης. ἀλλὰ μόνα ταῦτα εἰπόντες ἃ ἤκουσαν καὶ ἃ εἶδον ἁγίῳ πληρωθέντες πνεύματι. Συγγράμματα δὲ αὐτῶν ἔτι καὶ νῦν διαμένει, καὶ ἔστιν ἐντυχόντα τούτοις πλεῖστον ὠφεληθῆναι καὶ περὶ ἀρχῶν καὶ περὶ τέλους καὶ ὧν χρὴ εἰδέναι τὸν φιλόσοφον, πιστεύσαντα ἐκείνοις. Οὐ γὰρ μετὰ ἀποδείξεως πεποίηνται τότε τοὺς λόγους, ἃτε ἀνωτέρω πάσης ἀποδείξεως ὄντες ἀξιόπιστοι μάρτυρες τῆς ἀληθείας· τὰ δὲ ἀποβάντα καὶ ἀποβαίνοντα ἐξαναγκάζει συντίθεσθαι τοῖς λελαλημένοις δι᾿ αὐτῶν. Καίτοι γε καὶ διὰ τὰς δυνάμεις, ἃς ἐπετέλουν, πιστεύεσθαι δίκαιοι ἦσαν, ἐπειδὴ καὶ τὸν ποιητὴν τῶν ὅλων θεὸν καὶ πατέρα ἐδόξαζον καὶ τὸν παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ Χριστὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ κατήγγελλον· ὅπερ οἱ ἀπὸ τοῦ πλάνου καὶ ἀκαθάρτου πνεύματος ἐμπιπλάμενοι ψευδοπροφῆται οὕτε ἐποίησαν οὔτε ποιοῦσιν, ἀλλὰ δυνάμεις τινὰς ἐνεργεῖν εἰς κατάπληξιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων τολμῶσι καὶ τὰ τῆς πλάνης πνεύματα καὶ δαιμόνια δοξολογοῦσιν. Εὔχου δέ σοι πρὸ πάντων φωτὸς ἀνοιχθῆναι πύλας· οὐ γὰρ συνοπτὰ οὐδὲ συννοητὰ πᾶσίν ἐστιν, εἰ μή τῳ θεὸς δῷ συνιέναι καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς αὐτοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: What then, I say, would someone still need a teacher for, from where would someone be benefited, if not even in these things is the truth? There were certain people a long time ago before all of these supposed philosophers, older, blessed and righteous and loved by God, having spoken by divine Spirit and having ordained the things that are to come, which are now happening; and they call them prophets. These alone saw and spoke the truth to people, neither having been intimidated nor having been persuaded by someone, not having been overcome by glory. But having said only these things which they heard and which they saw, having been filled with holy Spirit. And their writings still remain even now, and it is possible for those who encounter these to be benefited the most, and to know about beginnings and about ends and about what the philosopher should know, having believed in them. For they did not establish their words with proof at that time, since being above all proof, they were trustworthy witnesses of the truth; and the things that have come to pass and are coming to pass compel one to agree with the things spoken through them. And indeed, even through the powers which they performed, they were worthy of being believed, since they also glorified the creator of all things, God and Father, and proclaimed the Christ who is from him, his Son; which the false prophets, filled with the deceitful and unclean spirit, neither did nor do, but they dare to perform certain powers for the amazement of people, and they glorify the spirits of deceit and demons. But I pray for you above all that the gates of light may be opened; for it is not visible or understandable to all, unless God gives understanding, and his Christ.

pass_b_english: What need, then, would anyone still have for a teacher, or from whom would anyone benefit, if the truth is not even found in these things?

Long before all these so-called philosophers, there were certain people—older, blessed, righteous, and beloved by God—who spoke by the divine Spirit and foretold the things that are to come, which are now happening; they are called prophets.

These alone both saw and spoke the truth to people, neither intimidated nor persuaded by anyone, not overcome by glory; they spoke only what they heard and what they saw, having been filled with the Holy Spirit.
Their writings still remain even now, and those who encounter them can benefit greatly—learning about beginnings and ends and what the philosopher ought to know—by believing them.

For they did not establish their words with proof at that time, since they were above all proof, being trustworthy witnesses of the truth; and the things that have come to pass and are coming to pass compel one to agree with the words spoken through them.

And indeed, even through the powers they performed, they were worthy of belief, since they glorified the Maker of all things, God and Father, and proclaimed the Christ from him, his Son—which the false prophets, filled with the deceitful and unclean spirit, neither did nor do; instead, they dare to perform certain powers to amaze people, and they glorify the spirits of deceit and demons.
But I pray for you above all that the gates of light may be opened; for these things are not visible or understandable to all, unless God gives understanding to someone, and his Christ.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the complex clauses regarding the prophets, the nature of their testimony, and the distinction between them and false prophets. The translation of 'ποιητὴν τῶν ὅλων' as 'creator of all things' (Pass A) and 'Maker of all things' (Pass B) is appropriate. The conditional structure at the end is preserved.
